title: Added New Theme color
summary: Bookmarks can now be **Black**, **Gray** or **White**, in addition to the six bright colors. Every bookmark color also gets a thin outline in a slightly darker (light mode) or lighter (dark mode) shade of its own color, and a subtle top-left to bottom-right shading, so pale bookmarks don't disappear into a light background and dark ones don't disappear into a dark background. This applies everywhere bookmark colors show: the color picker, the bookmark button above a chapter, the bookmarks list, the small marker on tabs, and the Today and Your content lists.

links.label: Issue 2040: Add black, gray and white bookmark colors, and give every bookmark a subtle outline and gradient

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Open the preview link above in a desktop browser (Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox). Use a private/incognito window for a clean start. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If it still looks like an older version, do a hard refresh: **Ctrl+Shift+R** (Windows) or **Cmd+Shift+R** (Mac).

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Bookmarks are only saved for signed-in users. Sign in with your email address and enter the code that is emailed to you.

setup.title: Make room for new bookmarks
setup.body: You can have at most **5** bookmarks. If your account already has 3 or more, open the bookmarks list (the **Bookmarks** button at the top of the Tabs list) and delete some with each bookmark's options menu → **Delete bookmark**, so you have room for 3 new ones. Note down the colors of any bookmarks you keep; a later test checks they didn't change.

setup.title: Start in the Light theme
setup.body: Make sure the app is in the **Light** theme (in **Settings** → **Themes**, or **Theme & text** on a phone). The tests switch to Dark later.

tests.title: The picker offers Black, Gray and White after the six bright colors
steps: Open **John 3**.
Click the bookmark button above the chapter (its label reads **Bookmark this chapter** when you hover over it).
If the panel lists existing bookmarks, click **New bookmark**.
Look at the row of round color swatches, and hover over each one to see its name.
expected: There are nine swatches, in this order: Orange, Red, Yellow, Green, Blue, Purple, **Black**, **Gray**, **White**.
Hovering over the last three shows the names **Black**, **Gray** and **White**.

tests.title: Every swatch has a thin edge and subtle shading, and White is clearly visible
tests.before: The new bookmark form from the previous test is still open.
steps: Look closely at the swatches (zoom the browser in with **Ctrl +** or **Cmd +** if it helps).
Click the **White** swatch to select it, then click **Orange**, then **White** again.
expected: Each swatch has a thin outline in a slightly darker shade of its own color, and is very slightly lighter at the top-left than at the bottom-right.
The White swatch has a soft gray edge and is easy to see against the light background.
The selected swatch still shows a clear ring around it, and the ring moves when you pick another color.

tests.title: A White bookmark can be saved and shows on the reader's bookmark button
tests.before: The new bookmark form is open on John 3 with **White** selected.
steps: Change the name to `White test`.
Click **Save**.
Close the bookmark panel and look at the bookmark button above John 3.
expected: The bookmark saves without an error message.
The bookmark button above the chapter now shows a white bookmark ribbon with a soft gray edge, clearly visible on the light page.
The ribbon is the same size as the button's empty bookmark outline was before you saved (it doesn't look bigger, smaller or cut off).

tests.title: Stacked bookmarks each get their own outline
tests.before: The `White test` bookmark from the previous section is on John 3.
steps: On **John 3**, click the bookmark button above the chapter, click **New bookmark**, pick **Black**, name it `Black test`, and click **Save**.
Do the same again with **Gray**, named `Gray test`.
Close the panel and look closely at the bookmark button above John 3 (zoom in if it helps).
expected: The button shows a small fanned-out stack of three ribbons: white, black and gray.
Each ribbon has its own thin edge that follows its tilt, and the small gaps between the ribbons are still there (they don't merge into one blob).
Hovering over the button shows **3 bookmarks on this chapter:** followed by the three names.

tests.title: The bookmarks list shows the new colors with outlines
steps: Open the Tabs list and click the **Bookmarks** button at its top (on a phone, it's also under the toolbar's **More** menu as **Bookmarks**).
Look at the icons next to `White test`, `Black test` and `Gray test`.
expected: Each bookmark's icon is in its color (white, black, gray) with a thin edge, and the white one is clearly visible.

tests.title: Changing a bookmark's color to a bright one shows the new outline too
steps: In the bookmarks list, open the options menu for `Gray test` and choose **Edit bookmark**.
Check the color swatches in the edit window, pick **Orange**, and click **Save**.
expected: The edit window shows the same nine swatches as the new bookmark form, with Gray selected when it opens.
After saving, `Gray test` shows an orange icon with a slightly deeper orange edge, in the list and on John 3's bookmark button.

tests.title: The small bookmark marker on a tab shows the outlined color
steps: Open the Tabs list and find the tab that's open on John 3.
Look at the small bookmark marker next to the tab's title (zoom in if it helps).
expected: A small bookmark marker appears next to the tab title, in the color of one of John 3's bookmarks, with a visible thin edge. Even if it's the white one, it's visible against the tab's background.
The marker isn't cut off and is the same small size as before.

tests.title: The Today and Your content lists show the new colors
steps: Open **Today** and scroll to the **BOOKMARKS** section.
Then open **Your content** and find the bookmarks.
expected: In both places, `White test` and `Black test` show white and black bookmark icons with thin edges, and both are clearly visible.

setup.title: Switch to the Dark theme
setup.body: Open **Settings** → **Themes** (or **Theme & text** on a phone) and choose **Dark**.

tests.title: Black and White bookmarks are both clearly visible in the Dark theme
steps: Open **John 3** and look at the bookmark button above the chapter.
Open the bookmarks list from the **Bookmarks** button at the top of the Tabs list.
Click the bookmark button above John 3 and click **New bookmark** to see the color swatches, then close it with **Discard new bookmark** (the ✕).
expected: The black bookmark has a lighter gray edge and stands out clearly from the dark background.
The white bookmark is still clearly visible.
Outlines on the other colors are slightly **lighter** than the color itself (in Light theme they were darker).
The swatches in the picker also have visible edges; the Black swatch doesn't disappear into the background.

setup.title: Use a phone, or a narrow window
setup.body: Open the preview on a phone (signed in to the same account), or make your browser window as narrow as it goes.

tests.title: All nine color swatches fit on a phone screen
steps: Open **John 3**, tap the bookmark button above the chapter, and tap **New bookmark**.
expected: All nine swatches are shown and can be tapped. If they don't fit on one line they wrap onto a second line; none are cut off and the page doesn't scroll sideways.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: The Bookmarks button at the top of the Tabs list keeps its own style
tests.why: Issue 2040 says this button is not affected; its look comes from issue 2039.
steps: Open the Tabs list and look at the **Bookmarks** button at its top while the bookmarks list is closed.
Click it to open the bookmarks list and look at the button again.
expected: With the list closed, the button shows plain line-drawn bookmark outlines, not the colored bookmarks.
With the list open, the button shows the bookmarks filled in one solid app highlight color, not each bookmark's own color, and without the new edges or shading.

tests.title: Bookmarks you already had keep their colors
tests.before: You noted the colors of any bookmarks you kept during setup. Skip this test if you had none.
steps: Open the bookmarks list and look at your older bookmarks.
expected: Each older bookmark is still the same color as before (now with a thin edge).

tests.title: Clean up
steps: Delete `White test`, `Black test` and `Gray test` from the bookmarks list (options menu → **Delete bookmark**, then confirm).
expected: Each bookmark disappears from the list, and John 3's bookmark button goes back to the empty outline.

notCovered: The exact outline width (1 screen pixel at every icon size) and the exact color mixing amounts can't be measured by eye; testers check that the edges look thin and consistent. These are covered by the PR's automated tests.
Translated color names in languages other than English: only the English names were added, translations come later.
Older app versions showing a new color as orange: that only happens on an older version of the app, which testers can't easily open.
